name: Asian Tuna Fritters with Pineapple-Cucumber Salad & Spicy Mayo (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 (1 inch) piece ginger root
½ small bunch green onion (scallion)
½ small bunch cilantro
½ small pineapple
1 English cucumber
½ lime

instructions.primary_message: Peel and mince ginger and garlic. Divide between a medium and a small bowl.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Divide between the two bowls with the ginger and garlic, then set the small bowl aside for later use.

Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the remaining medium bowl along with vinegar, sesame seeds, soy sauce, honey, and chili-garlic sauce. Stir to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tbsp rice vinegar
2 tsp sesame seeds
1 tsp soy sauce
1 tsp honey
½ tsp chili-garlic sauce

instructions.primary_message: Cut off skin from pineapple; quarter, core, and medium dice the flesh. Place a ½-cup on a plate for the kids. Add remaining pineapple to the bowl with the dressing.

Trim cucumber. Slice one-third crosswise into thin rounds, add to the plate with the pineapple, and set aside. Cut remaining cucumber into bite-sized pieces, add to the bowl, and stir to combine the salad. Set aside.

Drain tuna, place in another medium bowl, and flake with a fork. Add eggs, mayo, bread crumbs, salt, and pepper, then stir to combine. Using a scant ¼-cup measure, form four, ½-inch thick fritters for the kids. (Reserve remaining fritter batter for later use.)
instructions.secondary_message:
3 (6 oz) can chunk light tuna in water
3 tbsp mayonnaise
3 tbsp panko bread crumbs
⅛ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the kid fritters and pan-fry until golden and cooked through, 2-3 minutes per side. Remove to a plate. (Reserve skillet for later use.)

Meanwhile, add reserved ginger, garlic, and green onions to remaining fritter batter, along with soy sauce, and stir to combine the batter for the adults. Form batter into six, ½-inch thick fritters. (Reserve small bowl for the spicy mayo.)

Return the skillet to medium heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the adult fritters and pan-fry until golden and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Add to the plate with the kid's fritters, keeping them separate.
While the adult fritters are cooking, juice lime into the reserved small bowl. Add mayo, chili-garlic sauce, salt, and pepper, then stir to combine the spicy mayo.
instructions.secondary_message:
mayonnaise
2 tsp chili-garlic sauce
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message:
FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide the kid fritters, cucumber, and pineapple between plates. Serve with plain mayo for dipping. 

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide the adult fritters, spicy mayo, and salad between plates. Enjoy!
